title: My country
takeaway: My country is a picture of paradise, and it's ours to love and look after.
scene: A patriotic song with a repeated chorus: 'Eh mera desh jannat di tasveer ae', meaning 'This country of mine is a picture of paradise'. It reads like something children might sing at school on Independence Day.

original: ایہہ میرا دیش جنت دی تصویر اے
خلق چاہت محبت دی جاگیر اے
transliteration: Eh mera desh jannat di tasveer ae
Khalq chaahat mohabbat di jaageer ae
translation: This country of mine is a picture of paradise;
it's a homeland of kindness, affection and love.
couplets.story: The chorus: my country looks like a picture of paradise. It's a place full of kindness and love.

original: سب توں دھرتی اے سوہنی میرے دیش دی
مہک سب توں نیاری میرے دیش دی
transliteration: Sab ton dharti ae sohni mere desh di
Mehak sab ton niaari mere desh di
translation: My country's land is the most beautiful of all;
my country's fragrance is unlike any other.
couplets.story: His country's land is the most beautiful, and it has a smell all of its own.

original: ایہدی مٹی دی وکھری تاثیر اے
ایہہ میرا دیش جنت دی تصویر اے
transliteration: Ehdi mitti di vakhri taaseer ae
Eh mera desh jannat di tasveer ae
translation: Its soil has a special power of its own.
This country of mine is a picture of paradise.
couplets.story: There's something special about its soil. (Chorus.)

original: میرے دیش دا جواب نئیں جہان تے
اس دیش نوں مان اپنے جوان تے
transliteration: Mere desh da jawaab nahin jahaan te
Is desh nu maan apne javaan te
translation: There's nothing in the world to match my country;
this country is proud of its young people.
couplets.story: Nothing in the world compares to his country, and the country is proud of its young people.

original: ایہدی عظمت بنی ساڈی توقیر اے
ایہہ میرا دیش جنت دی تصویر اے
transliteration: Ehdi azmat bani saadi tauqeer ae
Eh mera desh jannat di tasveer ae
translation: Its greatness has become our honour.
This country of mine is a picture of paradise.
couplets.story: The country's greatness is what gives its people their dignity. (Chorus.)

original: ایہدے رکھاں تے فصلاں تے ساوا رنگ اے
ایس دیش دی مٹی بڑی اکسیر اے
transliteration: Ehde rukkhaan te faslaan te saava rang ae
Is desh di mitti bari akseer ae
translation: Its trees and crops are green;
the soil of this country is a magic cure.
couplets.story: Its trees and fields are green, and its soil is so good it's almost magical.

original: ایتھے لگن بہاراں دے میلے سدا
تا قیامت ایہنوں رکھے قائم خدا
transliteration: Ethe lagan bahaaraan de mele sada
Taa qiyaamat ehnu rakkhe qaaim Khuda
translation: May spring festivals always be held here;
may God keep it standing until the end of time.
couplets.story: May the country always be full of spring and celebration, and may God keep it safe until the end of the world.

original: ایہہ ساڈے ارماناں دی جاگیر اے
ساری ملت اس توں قربان ہے
transliteration: Eh saade armaanaan di jaageer ae
Saari millat is ton qurbaan hai
translation: It is the estate of all our hopes;
the whole nation would give everything for it.
couplets.story: It's where all their dreams live, and the whole nation would give anything for it.

original: ایہہ دھرتی پیاری پاکستان ہے
اسی رانجھے ایہدے ساڈی ایہہ ہیر اے
transliteration: Eh dharti pyaari Pakistan hai
Asi Raanjhe ehde, saadi eh Heer ae
translation: This beloved land is Pakistan;
we are its Ranjhas, and it is our Heer.
couplets.story: This beloved land is Pakistan. Then a lovely image: we are like Ranjha, the famous lover, and our country is our Heer, the one we love.

original: ایہدے جشن آزادی مناندے رہیے
وانگ جنت ایہہ گلشن سجاندے رہیے
transliteration: Ehde jashn-e-azaadi manaande rahiye
Vaang jannat eh gulshan sajaande rahiye
translation: Let's keep celebrating its Independence Day;
let's keep decorating this garden like paradise.
couplets.story: Let's keep celebrating our independence, and keep making our country as beautiful as paradise.

original: شاعر مشرق دے خواباں دی تعبیر اے
ایہدا پرچم میں احمدؔ جھلاندا رواں
transliteration: Shaair-e-Mashriq de khwaabaan di taabeer ae
Ehda parcham main Ahmad jhulaanda ravaan
translation: It is the dream of the Poet of the East come true.
May I, Ahmad, keep waving its flag.
couplets.story: Pakistan is the dream of Iqbal, 'the Poet of the East', come true. The poet wants to keep waving its flag forever.

original: ایہدی چاہت دے نغمے سناندا رواں
ساڈے قائد نے بخشی ایہہ جاگیر اے
transliteration: Ehdi chaahat de naghme sunaanda ravaan
Saade Quaid ne bakhshi eh jaageer ae
translation: May I keep singing songs of love for it.
Our Leader gave us this homeland as a gift.
couplets.story: He wants to keep singing songs about how much he loves it. This homeland was a gift from Jinnah, their great leader.

deeper: Mostly a love song for Pakistan. Faith appears in one prayer: 'may God keep it standing until the end of time'. Calling the country 'our Heer' borrows the great Sufi love story, but here it is about loving a homeland, not about God.
why: A simple, joyful patriotic song. The line 'we are its Ranjhas and it is our Heer' connects love of country to Punjab's greatest love story.
prompt: What do you love most about the place you come from?
notes: The chorus line is repeated after each verse in the book; here it is shown only where it falls in the couplet pairs.
